title: Citi Cuts Bitcoin Target 12% to $99,532 as Ethereum Forecast Falls to $2,838
body: Key takeaways Citi cuts Bitcoin's 12-month forecast nearly 12% Ethereum target falls to $2,838 amid weaker demand ETF withdrawals challenge Wall Street's cryptocurrency recovery expectations Citigroup has reportedly lowered its 12-month Bitcoin price target from $113,000 to $99,532, a nearly 12% reduction, while cutting its Ethereum forecast from $3,028 to $2,838 as institutional demand weakens. The November 18 revisions, reported by CNBC and attributed to Citi analyst Alex Saunders, mark a sharp reversal from the bank's October optimism. Bitcoin was trading around $64,000-$65,000 on Wednesday, while Ethereum remained near $1,800 following another difficult week for cryptocurrency markets. Despite the downgrades, Citi's revised targets still imply substantial upside. Bitcoin would need to gain approximately 55% from $64,000 to reach $99,532, while Ethereum would require a roughly 58% recovery from $1,800 to reach $2,838. Why Citi Cut Its Bitcoin and Ethereum Forecasts Citi's latest revisions follow a deterioration in exchange-traded fund demand, weaker cryptocurrency market activity and a less supportive macroeconomic environment. The bank had previously raised its Bitcoin forecast from $82,000 to $113,000 in early October, citing renewed ETF inflows and improving financial conditions. Ethereum received a similar upgrade, with Citi lifting its ETH price target from $2,240 to $3,028. Those conditions have since deteriorated. Bitcoin has fallen below its 200-day moving average, a closely watched indicator used to assess broader market momentum. Citi's revised outlook reflects reduced expectations for near-term capital inflows, according to reports citing the bank's latest analysis. The reversal also follows an earlier Citi downgrade in July , illustrating how rapidly institutional cryptocurrency forecasts have changed during 2026. Bitcoin ETFs Lose $240 Million as Institutional Demand Weakens The latest ETF data provides additional context for Citi's decision. According to Farside Investors , US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $239.9 million in net withdrawals on November 17, reversing the previous session's $7.9 million inflow. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $209.5 million of the withdrawals, highlighting the selling pressure affecting the largest institutional Bitcoin investment products. The decline follows a prolonged November Bitcoin ETF selloff that has complicated BTC's attempts to establish support above $65,000. Ethereum funds face similar challenges. US spot ETH ETFs lost $29.1 million on November 17, including $27.6 million from BlackRock's ETHA, according to Farside's Ethereum data . The withdrawals follow an earlier $144.8 million Ethereum ETF outflow , reinforcing concerns about the sustainability of institutional demand. ETF redemptions are not the only factor influencing cryptocurrency prices, but repeated withdrawals can weaken an important source of buying interest. Bitcoin and Ethereum Price Predictions: Can Crypto Recover? Citi's new targets remain substantially above current market prices, suggesting that the bank has reduced its expectations without abandoning its longer-term recovery scenario. For Bitcoin, the immediate challenge is stabilizing above $64,000 and reclaiming $65,000. A stronger recovery could bring $70,000 back into focus, although another decline toward $62,000 remains possible if selling persists. Ethereum faces a similar test around $1,800, with $1,900 representing an initial recovery objective before the psychologically important $2,000 level. Recent Ethereum price weakness shows how difficult sustained rebounds have become despite continued institutional accumulation elsewhere in the market.

title: Monero’s FCMP++ cryptographic upgrade passes zkSecurity audit with no major flaws
body: BitcoinWorld Monero’s FCMP++ cryptographic upgrade passes zkSecurity audit with no major flaws Monero’s effort to overhaul its privacy technology cleared a key checkpoint on Nov. 18, when zkSecurity published the results of an audit of the Generalized Bulletproofs code underlying the planned FCMP++ upgrade, finding no high or medium severity vulnerabilities, according to Crypto.news . The audit, commissioned by nonprofit research funder MAGIC Grants in June, examined the generalized-bulletproofs crate within monero-oxide, a Rust implementation of Monero’s cryptographic components. zkSecurity found four low severity issues and three informational findings in Monero’s Generalized Bulletproofs implementation, with no high or medium severity flaws. The monero-oxide developers have responded to all seven findings, and zkSecurity separately published a machine-checked proof confirming the protocol’s completeness, zero-knowledge, and soundness properties. Key facts zkSecurity conducted the audit over ten working days, led by researchers Mathias Hall-Andersen and Suneal Gong. The review identified four low severity issues and three informational findings, all of which received responses from the monero-oxide developers. MAGIC Grants commissioned the audit in June to examine the generalized-bulletproofs crate within monero-oxide, a Rust implementation of Monero’s cryptographic components. zkSecurity also formalized the protocol’s mathematical properties using the Lean theorem prover and published the work in a public GitHub repository. Monero confirmed the audit results in a Nov. 18 statement on X, quoting the findings published by MAGIC Grants. What the mathematical verification covers Beyond the code review, zkSecurity’s researchers developed a new mathematical proof of knowledge soundness, a property that ensures a participant cannot produce a valid proof without possessing the required underlying information. The team formalized completeness, zero-knowledge, and soundness using Lean, a theorem prover that allows computers to check each step in a mathematical argument. Those three properties are central to Monero’s privacy guarantees. Completeness means valid proofs are accepted, zero-knowledge ensures the verification process does not reveal the secret being proved, and soundness prevents invalid statements from being accepted as legitimate. The formal verification covered the interactive protocol in an abstract mathematical group, while the written audit addressed the implementation and related cryptographic components. The researchers also examined two more efficient variants of Generalized Bulletproofs during the formalization, though Monero has no immediate plans to adopt either version. How FCMP++ changes Monero’s privacy model The audit forms part of Monero’s continuing work on FCMP++, a planned network upgrade intended to change how the blockchain proves that funds being spent belong to its existing transaction history. Currently, Monero uses ring signatures to conceal which transaction output is actually being spent. FCMP++ would replace that approach with membership proofs covering the blockchain’s entire output set. The proposed system would allow transactions to draw from an anonymity set covering approximately 150 million existing outputs, instead of relying on the smaller groups used by ring signatures. Monero launched its second FCMP++ beta stressnet on May 6 at block height 2,997,100, as Crypto.news previously reported. Security work on the upgrade has involved several independent assessments. MAGIC Grants announced a separate audit of the FCMP++ cryptographic implementation by Trail of Bits on Aug. 17. Community funding has supported development alongside those reviews; in October, a Monero developer requested 45 XMR for three months of work covering core software, wallet improvements, and privacy infrastructure. Monero’s Community Crowdfunding System had previously funded a separate 500 XMR audit of FCMP++ integration. Why it matters For Monero users, the audit reduces uncertainty around a component that would sit at the core of the network’s next major privacy upgrade. Anonymity set size is a key factor in how resistant a privacy coin is to chain analysis, and moving from ring signatures to full-chain membership proofs would represent a structural shift rather than an incremental improvement. The review also adds a formal verification layer that goes beyond typical code audits, giving developers a mathematical basis for the protocol’s security claims. Because Monero relies on community-backed funding for research and audits, the completion of this review may affect how future upgrade work is sequenced and financed. Market snapshot Monero (XMR) traded at $505 (₹47,222) on Nov. 18, 2026, down 0.6% over 24 hours and 12.4% over the past seven days, according to CoinPaprika data timestamped 10:30 UTC. Its market capitalization stood at $9.52 billion with 24-hour volume of $161.9 million. What to watch The next signals will come from the FCMP++ beta stressnet and the separate Trail of Bits audit announced by MAGIC Grants on Aug. 17; any findings from that review, and the developers’ responses to them, will shape the timeline for the upgrade’s activation. Frequently Asked Questions What is the FCMP++ upgrade in Monero? FCMP++ is a planned Monero network upgrade that would replace the current ring signature system with Full-Chain Membership Proofs, allowing transactions to draw from the entire set of existing outputs rather than smaller decoy groups. Who conducted the audit of Monero’s Generalized Bulletproofs code? The audit was commissioned by MAGIC Grants and carried out by zkSecurity researchers Mathias Hall-Andersen and Suneal Gong over ten working days. How many findings were raised in the zkSecurity audit? zkSecurity identified four low severity issues and three informational findings, all of which received responses from the monero-oxide developers. Has Monero responded to the audit findings? Yes, the monero-oxide developers have responded to all seven findings. Monero also confirmed the successful audit in a Nov. 18 statement on X, highlighting zkSecurity’s additional mathematical verification work. title: CertiK verifies XRP Ledger and Partior self-attestations under Global Layer One toolkit
body: Blockchain security firm CertiK said it has completed independent verification of XRP Ledger Foundation and Partior’s filed self-attestations under the Global Layer One Market Infrastructure Toolkit. The CertiK review of the Ripple-linked network and Partior announced Wednesday, November 18, is the first visible result since the project was taken over by a bank-run standards body two weeks ago. What is the GL1 review that XRP Ledger passed? The GL1 MI Toolkit is a framework of 112 controls that allows financial institutions and market infrastructure operators to use self-attestations or independent auditor verifications to grade the suitability of their digital financial infrastructures. The Toolkit, now at version 2.0, runs on a framework grounded in international standards and industry best practices. The 112 controls on theGL1 MI Toolkit. Source: GL1 Market Infrastructure (MI) Toolkit According to CertiK’s account of its XRP Ledger and Partior verifications, the blockchain security firm reviewed all 112 controls in the GL1 MI Toolkit to determine which ones it could verify independently. Next, it checked both projects’ claims against the Toolkit’s Architecture and Resiliency principles, drawing on code, configurations, logs, and test results to assess whether the controls were built as described. CertiK’s independent verifications of XRP Ledger and Partior join other network self-attestations, such as Base, HSBC Orion, Kinexys by J.P. Morgan and Solana listed on the GL site. XRP Ledger and Partior are the first networks to have their self-attestations independently verified by CertiK. Source:GL1 Market Infrastructure (MI) Toolkit CertiK’s Head of Capital Markets and Policy Esme Pau emphasized the importance of independent verification, writing in the November 18 statement, “Independent technical verification helps operators substantiate their self-attestations and gives institutions evidence they can weigh in their own infrastructure assessments.” Banks take over GL1 from Singapore’s MAS GL1 went from an initiative convened by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) three years ago under Project Guardian to Global Layer One Organisation, a Singapore non-profit announced on November 4 by HSBC, Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, MUFG Bank, Societe Generale-FORGE and Standard Chartered when they over framework governance. The announcement also noted that the bank-led body will be open to banks, fintechs, market infrastructure providers and policymakers. GL1 founders had to scale back their ambitions of creating a shared open ledger for regulated finance over intellectual property concerns. The framework they went forward with contained two toolkits: One for assessing whether they can connect with a network The other for programmable compliance The MI Toolkit itself was launched in November 2025 with legal input from firms including Linklaters, which said it advised GL1 on the framework’s development . What the CertiK verification means for XRPL’s institutional pitch XRP Ledger is a public blockchain that launched in 2012 and is closely tied to Ripple, built for payments, token issuance and on-chain trading. Going through the same controls check used by bank-connected networks fits a run of institutional moves on the ledger. Earlier in 2026, XRPL activated XLS-81, a “permissioned DEX” that lets approved institutions run gated trading venues with know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering controls, alongside XLS-85, which extended native escrow to stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets. Ripple also joined JPMorgan, Mastercard and Ondo Finance in a cross-border tokenized U.S. Treasury redemption that settled the asset leg on XRPL while banks handled the cash, Cryptopolitan reported earlier this year. title: Bitcoin price today: BTC below $64,000 as Citi cuts target to $99,532
body: Key takeaways Bitcoin traded below $64,000 as Citi cut its 12-month target to $99,532. US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $239.9 million on Tuesday, led by BlackRock's IBIT. Minutes from the Fed's October meeting are due at 19:00 UK time. Bitcoin price today slipped further below $64,000 on Wednesday, November 18, after Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin target to $99,532 and as US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung back to outflows ahead of the Federal Reserve's October minutes. Bitcoin (BTC) traded at $63,465 on Coinbase at 15:08 UK time, down 2.2% from Tuesday's close of $64,873 at midnight UTC. Citi cuts its 12-month Bitcoin and Ethereum targets Citi cut its 12-month Bitcoin price target to $99,532 from $113,000 and its Ethereum target to $2,838 from $3,028, according to a research note reported by CNBC on Wednesday. Citi analyst Alex Saunders said a rangebound crypto market had broken lower and that both assets had fallen since the bank's previous update. He downgraded Citi's near-term outlook for capital inflows to neutral after Bitcoin dropped below its 200-day moving average. Saunders pointed to weaker ETF demand, with Bitcoin fund flows in net outflow so far this year and Ethereum funds recording outflows in each of the past seven weeks. Futures positioning pointed to broader deleveraging, he said, while a stronger US dollar, higher real yields and a rise in equity-market volatility had tightened the backdrop for crypto. Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 is again running above its correlation with gold, according to the note. Citi had raised those targets to $113,000 and $3,028 in early October. Even after the cut, the new Bitcoin target implies about 57% upside from Wednesday's Coinbase price. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, leaving about 60% implied upside to Citi's $2,838 Ethereum target. What happened to Bitcoin price today? Bitcoin traded between $63,001 and $64,933 on Coinbase on Wednesday, with sellers capping every move towards $65,000. The world's largest cryptocurrency is about 16% below its November 9 high of $75,500 on Coinbase. It hit $61,946 on Coinbase on November 15, its lowest point of the month so far. The rest of the market was also lower. Ether traded at $1,769 on Coinbase, while XRP was at $0.98. Bitcoin price chart | Source: Coinbase Why is Bitcoin price falling? ETF demand has faded again, the same pressure Citi cited in its target cut. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $239.9 million on Tuesday, November 17, according to Farside Investors . BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $209.5 million of that. That reversed a small $7.9 million inflow on Monday. Since October 30, the funds have lost about $3.2 billion in 13 sessions, based on Farside's daily data. US spot Ether ETFs lost $29.1 million on Tuesday, Farside data show. Interest rates are the other weight. The Fed held its target range at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, but Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike . On Tuesday, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy "will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027", in remarks in Argentina. Higher rates make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive. The US dollar index touched a 52-week high of 103.91 on Wednesday, according to TradingView. What happens next? The Fed's minutes from its October 27-28 meeting are due at 19:00 UK time on Wednesday. Traders will look at how many officials backed a hike and how soon. The Fed's next decision is on December 9. Bitfinex analysts said in their Bitfinex Alpha report on Monday that they expect Bitcoin to trade between $61,800 and $69,400 this week, with another test of the November 15 low possible. They named $57,803, Bitcoin's July cycle low, as a key level to watch, and said a recovery above $72,700 with renewed ETF inflows would show selling pressure is fading. Farside's figures for Wednesday's ETF flows will show whether institutional selling has eased. Should you buy Bitcoin now? Bitcoin has held above last week's low, but ETF outflows and a hawkish Fed are still weighing on it. Citi's reduced 12-month target of $99,532 still sits well above the current price, though that is a forecast, not a recommendation. A hawkish set of minutes could push Bitcoin back towards $62,000, while a softer tone could bring buyers back. title: Cardano Founder Charles Hoskinson Teases Surprise Midnight Announcements for December 15
tags: Market|Charles Hoskinson News|Latest Cardano (ADA) Crypto News Today
body: Charles Hoskinson confirms a December 15 Midnight presentation, promising surprise announcements and a preview of the blockchain’s 2027 plans. Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has confirmed plans for a major Midnight presentation on December 15, 2026, promising a review of the privacy-focused blockchain’s progress and several surprise announcements concerning its future. Speaking during a November 17 video titled December 15th and Closing Out the Year , Hoskinson revealed that the event would outline Midnight’s development priorities for 2027. “On December 15th, we’re going to talk about Midnight’s year in review and what’s coming in 2027,” Hoskinson stated. He added that the Midnight Foundation, Shielded Technologies, and Input Output have been preparing several developments for the upcoming year. “We have a lot of incredible things queued up, and some surprise announcements,” he said. Hoskinson Confirms December 15 Midnight Presentation The December 15 presentation will focus on Midnight’s achievements throughout 2026 and provide a preview of the project’s next development phase. Hoskinson indicated that the presentation would use a keynote-style format, with slides outlining the technology, products, and broader direction of the ecosystem. The announcement follows his November 15 update revealing that development teams were working extensively on Midnight’s next roadmap phase. He confirmed that Sebastien Guillemot had traveled to Colorado to collaborate with the team, while developers at the Midnight Foundation and Shielded Technologies were advancing their respective projects. However, Hoskinson has not disclosed the specifics of the promised surprise announcements. Midnight Already Has Major Developments Planned for 2027 Although the surprise announcements remain undisclosed, Midnight’s existing roadmap identifies several upgrades scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Among the most significant is NIGHT staking, which would allow token holders to delegate their assets to stake pools and earn rewards for participating in network security. The roadmap also targets opening block production to Cardano stake pool operators, expanding decentralization beyond Midnight’s current federated infrastructure. Another planned development is the gradual migration toward the BABE consensus mechanism, alongside improvements in zero-knowledge proof generation and transaction processing. These features are scheduled roadmap objectives, not newly confirmed December 15 announcements. Hoskinson has previously expressed considerable optimism about Midnight’s growth prospects. As The Crypto Basic reported in September , he expects 2027 to be a significant expansion year, highlighting privacy-focused AI agents, decentralized finance, and cross-chain infrastructure. Midnight Enters December After Major 2026 Milestones The upcoming presentation follows several important achievements during 2026. Midnight officially launched its mainnet in March, while permissionless smart contract deployment became available in September. On November 6, the network completed its Ledger 9 upgrade, introducing additional signature support, contract composability, and security improvements. Another major milestone followed on November 16, when Monument Bank launched interest-bearing tokenized deposits on Midnight. The initial phase targets up to £250 million in customer deposits, although that figure represents the program’s intended scale rather than confirmation that the full amount has already been tokenized. As The Crypto Basic previously covered , Hoskinson considers the banking initiative an early step toward bringing more traditional financial assets onto Midnight. What Midnight’s Announcements Could Mean for Cardano Hoskinson has repeatedly emphasized Midnight’s importance to the Cardano ecosystem. He recently defended Midnight’s connection to Cardano , pointing to NIGHT’s original issuance on Cardano and the planned participation of Cardano stake pool operators. Although Midnight operates its own blockchain, Hoskinson views its expansion as complementary to Cardano’s broader ecosystem. The December 15 event will therefore provide further detail on Midnight’s growth strategy, including how its existing roadmap will develop through 2027. For now, the date and presentation plans are confirmed by Hoskinson’s statements, while the content of the surprise announcements remains undisclosed.

title: Nvidia Earnings Surge as Board Rejects Huang’s Return and Bitcoin Eyes $60K
tags: Bitcoin News|News|bitcoin price|btc price|Jensen Huang|nvidia ceo|nvidia earnings|nvidia earnings surge
body: Nvidia earnings delivered a fresh boost to market sentiment after the chipmaker reported record quarterly revenue and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook. The results helped lift technology stocks and supported Bitcoin’s recovery, although concerns surrounding the broader crypto market remain. The positive earnings report came alongside a major leadership development: Nvidia’s board rejected calls to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang , despite his public willingness to return. Meanwhile, Bitcoin continued trading within a narrow range as investors monitored liquidity around the $60,000 level. Nvidia Earnings Beat Expectations Despite Leadership Turmoil Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, representing a 103% increase from the same period last year. The figure exceeded analyst expectations of $109.3 billion by approximately 5.6%, highlighting continued demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Data center revenue more than doubled to $107.6 billion, accounting for roughly 93% of the company’s total sales. The chipmaker also provided an optimistic outlook for the current quarter, projecting revenue of approximately $130 billion. That compares with Wall Street expectations of around $125.3 billion, suggesting that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains strong. However, the financial performance came amid uncertainty surrounding the company’s leadership. Board chairman Harvey Jones confirmed during the earnings call that directors had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. The announcement followed Huang’s earlier statement that he would be honored to return if the board believed it was in shareholders’ best interests. Nvidia shares initially closed 0.4% lower at $155.46 on Tuesday before gaining approximately 4% in after-hours trading following the earnings announcement. Bitcoin Recovers as Nvidia Boosts Market Sentiment Nvidia’s results provided some relief across financial markets, with Bitcoin recovering into its recent $64,000–$66,000 trading range. The cryptocurrency had briefly slipped below that range on Tuesday ahead of Nvidia’s earnings announcement, extending concerns following its recent decline toward $62,000, an 18-week low recorded over the weekend. The improvement in sentiment also extended to traditional markets. Nvidia shares gained approximately 3% in Wednesday premarket trading, while Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 1%. South Korea’s KOSPI Composite also climbed 2%, closing at 5,067 points and recovering above the closely watched 5,000 threshold. Although the developments suggest renewed confidence in technology-related assets, Bitcoin’s recovery remains relatively limited. Investors are still assessing liquidity conditions, interest-rate expectations and the possibility of further downside across risk markets. Glassnode Identifies $60K as Critical Bitcoin Liquidity Zone Despite Bitcoin’s stabilization , market participants continue watching the $60,000 level as an important area for potential support. According to Glassnode, Binance and Coinbase order-book data show that resting buy orders within 5% of Bitcoin’s current price outweigh sell orders by approximately 2.3 times. The research firm also identified the $60,000 region as the largest individual bid concentration on Binance since August. This suggests that buyers are positioning themselves around the level, potentially providing a cushion if selling pressure returns. However, Glassnode warned that a move toward $60,000 could trigger additional liquidations among traders holding leveraged long positions, potentially accelerating a decline. The firm added that most forced position closures had already occurred during the initial sell-off. For now, Nvidia’s earnings have offered a temporary improvement in market sentiment, but Bitcoin still needs to establish stronger support before a sustained recovery becomes clearer. Could Nvidia’s strong earnings help Bitcoin regain its bullish momentum, or will broader market uncertainty continue weighing on prices? body: Nvidia has stopped shipping its licensed Hopper AI chips to China, raising questions about an export deal arranged by President Donald Trump. Interim CEO Colette Kress announced the decision during Tuesday’s earnings call. She said Nvidia sold $2.4 billion worth of these chips to China in the three months ended October 25. The company has now removed that amount from its quarterly sales forecast. Kress did not explain why the shipments had stopped or whether they would resume. The Hopper range includes the H200 chip, which is used to train and run large AI models. The chips are made in Taiwan by TSMC, the world’s largest chip manufacturer for other companies. Trump-brokered deal now in doubt The US had already started easing its rules on selling these chips to China. After meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping last year, President Donald Trump agreed to allow H200 sales to approved Chinese companies. In January, the US began accepting applications to sell the chips to China , under certain security rules, according to the Economic Times. The deal also included a 25% tariff on approved chips sent through the US before reaching China. Reuters previously reported that 10 Chinese companies, including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, had received approval to buy the chips. However, China has restricted imports as it tries to depend less on US technology. Reuters reported that about 600,000 H200 chips were still in Hong Kong earlier this month, waiting for approval from China. Nvidia’s more powerful Blackwell and Rubin chips also remain banned from China because of US national security concerns. The scandal involved Nvidia’s decision comes as the company faces problems over former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who some US officials reportedly suspect of spying for China. Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, once ran Megaspeed International, a company based in Singapore. Megaspeed is under investigation over claims that it helped Chinese firms buy Nvidia chips illegally, breaking US export rules. The controversy has also hurt Nvidia’s market value. The US has also tightened its rules on chip exports. On Monday, it took new steps to stop chips from being smuggled into China. According to AFP, the measures also target Chinese companies that rent computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia that use powerful Nvidia chips. Don’t just read crypto news. Understand it. title: Banking giant sets Bitcoin (BTC) price target for 2027
body: Citi has lowered its 12-month Bitcoin ( BTC ) price target, scaling back its outlook for the largest cryptocurrency due to changing expectations for spot exchange-traded fund ( ETF ) inflows. Specifically, the bank now sees Bitcoin reach $99,532 in the next year, significantly below the previous prediction of $113,000 set in early October, when the bank was optimistic regarding institutional flows and development surrounding the CLARITY Act. However, with Bitcoin trading at approximately $63,580, the revised target still implies nearly 60% upside potential in the specified period, and it largely agrees with some other recent projections , which suggest BTC could enter an accumulation phase before reaching $100,000-$120,000 by late 2027. Changes in expected fund inflows can therefore translate directly into adjustments to its price projections. For example, in July this year, Citi established a $82,000 BTC price forecast, based on an assumption of zero net inflows. By October, however, improving expectations prompted the bank to raise those targets to $113,000. However, its November forecasts again reflect a more cautious outlook, with the bank now estimating $5 billion in net inflows into cryptocurrency investment products. That figure represents a notable revision from the earlier $10 billion estimate. From this it also follows that stronger-than-expected ETF demand could support higher price projections down the line, while weaker flows could, of course, lead to further price cuts. The $63,111–$64,373 region is particularly significant because Bitcoin has already experienced a substantial correction throughout November. title: Abu Dhabi Funds Hold $1.09B in Bitcoin ETF, Q3 Filings Show
tags: Bitcoin|ETFs|13F filings|Bitcoin ETF|IBIT|sovereign wealth|Swiss National Bank
body: BitcoinWorld Abu Dhabi Funds Hold $1.09B in Bitcoin ETF, Q3 Filings Show Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala Investment Company and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council together held about $1.09 billion in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) at the close of the third quarter, according to the quarterly Form 13F disclosures the two institutions filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in mid-November. The filing period also brought large position increases from hedge fund Brevan Howard and market maker Susquehanna International Group, Crypto.news reported on November 18. The Q3 2026 13F filings show Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council holding roughly $1.09 billion of BlackRock’s IBIT between them, with no change in share count. Brevan Howard raised its IBIT position by 211% to $1.06 billion, and the Swiss National Bank reported about $227 million in Bitcoin-linked equities. Key facts Mubadala disclosed 14,721,917 IBIT shares worth about $696.94 million; the Abu Dhabi Investment Council listed 8,218,712 shares valued at $389.07 million, for a combined 22.94 million shares. Neither Abu Dhabi fund changed its IBIT share count during the quarter; the reported value of the combined position rose from about $763.69 million at the end of June to roughly $1.09 billion at the end of September. Brevan Howard reported 22,405,494 IBIT shares worth $1.06 billion, up from 7,205,004 shares worth $239.85 million in June — a 211% increase in share count. Susquehanna disclosed about $622 million across spot Bitcoin ETFs, including 9,124,511 IBIT shares valued at $431.95 million, compared with 2,312,996 shares worth $77 million in June. The Swiss National Bank reported about $227 million across Strategy and nine Bitcoin mining and infrastructure firms, including $109.32 million of Strategy shares and $117.71 million of the mining-related names. What the filings show across institutions The value of the Abu Dhabi holdings climbed without any new buying at quarter-end. Mubadala’s IBIT position moved from $490.09 million at the end of June to $696.94 million, while the council’s went from $273.60 million to $389.07 million. For the council, IBIT made up around 54% of the $716.87 million it disclosed through Form 13F, the largest single line in its reported U.S. securities portfolio. Brevan Howard’s increase was the sharpest change among the large holders. Its November filing shows a net addition of more than 15.2 million IBIT shares over three months. The hedge fund separately disclosed call options on 5.48 million IBIT shares and put options covering 517,600 shares, which are not counted in its $1.06 billion shareholding. Susquehanna’s IBIT share count surged 294%. Beyond BlackRock, its filing listed about $70.60 million in the Grayscale Bitcoin Trust ETF, $58.21 million in Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund and $27.54 million in the Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF, alongside sizable call and put positions consistent with its market-making and derivatives business. The Swiss National Bank’s passive equity exposure The Swiss central bank’s November 12 filing listed 714,100 Strategy shares worth $109.32 million, up from $64.01 million in June even though it cut 22,200 shares during the quarter. Its other exposures included $38.96 million in IREN, $17.23 million in Hut 8, $13.83 million in Riot Platforms and $11.49 million in TeraWulf. Adding Cipher Digital, Core Scientific, MARA Holdings, CleanSpark and Bitdeer brought the nine mining-related names to about $117.71 million. The SNB describes these as passive investments in listed companies, not Bitcoin ownership, and says it does not select individual equities. Why it matters The filings are the clearest public check on who was holding Bitcoin-linked exposure through the third quarter, and they put sovereign and central-bank-adjacent institutions alongside hedge funds in the same BlackRock product. For retail investors who track institutional flows as a signal, the pattern is worth noting: two of the largest holders stood still while the ETF’s value rose, which means their reported gains came from price, not purchases. The disclosures land after a weak stretch for the asset, with Bitcoin at $63,897 on November 18, down 13.1% over seven days. Market snapshot Bitcoin traded at $63,897 (₹5,969,610) at the November 18 timestamp, down 1.6% over 24 hours and 13.1% over seven days, with a market cap of $1.29 trillion and 24-hour volume of $18.75 billion, per CoinPaprika data. Ether was at $1,790 (₹167,234), down 12.9% on the week. What to watch The next Form 13F round, covering positions as of December 31, 2026, is due on February 16, 2027. Between now and then, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $1.28 billion in net withdrawals during November 2–6 and another $1.07 billion the following week, which will inform how much of the Q3 positioning was held through the November selloff toward $62,000 on November 15. Frequently Asked Questions What does a Form 13F filing show about Bitcoin ETF holdings? It is a quarterly report institutions with at least $100 million in U.S. securities must file with the SEC, listing their positions as of the quarter’s end. The Q3 filings snapshot holdings as of September 30, 2026. Did Abu Dhabi funds add to their Bitcoin ETF position in Q3? No. Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council kept their quarter-end IBIT share counts unchanged. The reported value rose from about $763.69 million to roughly $1.09 billion because of price appreciation. Does the Swiss National Bank hold Bitcoin directly? Its filing lists shares of Bitcoin-treasury company Strategy and several mining companies. Those are positions in publicly traded equities, not direct Bitcoin ownership, and the SNB says it invests passively and does not select equities. When will the next Bitcoin ETF holdings data be released? The next Form 13F round, covering positions as of December 31, 2026, is due on February 16, 2027. title: Most non-custodial wallets fall short for wealthy holders on inheritance and multi-user access, Bron report finds
body: Most non-custodial crypto wallets lack the inheritance and shared-access tools that wealthy holders and family offices need, according to a scored comparison prepared by wallet provider Bron . Of the ten wallets assessed, four offer no inheritance feature at all, and six are single-user products. What the report assessed Bron’s report scores ten wallets on twelve criteria worth 100 points in total. It is aimed at affluent and high-net-worth individuals and family offices. Alongside Bron’s own wallet, it covers Ledger, MetaMask, MPC Vault, Phantom, Safe, Tangem, Trezor, Trust Wallet and Zengo. Security carries the most weight at 15 points. Multi-user management and inheritance are worth 10 points each. The sections below cover those two first, then the overall scores and the full list of criteria. Bron says its claims trace to vendors’ official documentation and help centers. It adds that it cross-checked them in live tests, in which each vendor’s support desk answered the same questions on recovery, inheritance, team access, and limits. Total points out of 100. Source: Bron Inheritance: four wallets have no feature Inheritance carries 10 of the 100 points. Trust Wallet, Phantom, MetaMask, and MPC Vault scored zero, with no beneficiary designation and no dormancy mechanism. According to the report, their support desks confirmed that an heir who does not hold the credential inherits nothing. Ledger, Trezor, and Tangem scored two points each. Ledger points users to third-party services or Ledger Multisig, and Trezor to multisig partners. For Tangem, the report treats handing over a backup card and access code as handing over a live key, and scored it the same two points as Ledger. Only three wallets scored above that. Bron’s Digital Inheritance feature scored 10: a designated beneficiary starts a claim, which runs a 12-month delay, shortened to six months if the beneficiary enters codes from two guardians. The owner, a guardian, or a beneficiary can cancel at any time. Zengo’s Legacy Transfer, a paid Pro feature, scored 9. It releases access to one recipient after an inactivity timer of 3 to 24 months. Safe scored 6, because a designated recoverer can replace the signers after a review delay, but only as a do-it-yourself setup on EVM chains. Shared control: six single-user wallets Multi-user management also carries 10 points. The report says Trust Wallet, MetaMask, Phantom, Tangem, Trezor and, in its consumer app, Ledger are single-user products. According to the report, their support desks confirmed that the only way to share control is to share the key itself. Bron scored 10, ahead of MPC Vault and Zengo with 9 each, and Ledger and Safe with 7. Ledger’s score rests on separate products, Ledger Multisig and Ledger Enterprise. Bron says Zengo’s roles sit in a separate business app, which cost it a point. Overall scores Bron placed first with 84 points, followed by Ledger (72), Zengo (70), Trezor (58), Tangem and Trust Wallet (51 each), MetaMask (49), MPC Vault (43), and Phantom and Safe (42 each). On security, the report’s largest weighting at 15 points, Bron and Safe scored full marks. Zengo scored 14. Trust Wallet, MetaMask and Phantom scored 6 each. Bron says that is because they authorize transactions with a password or biometric on the same device that holds the key, and a lost recovery phrase cannot be recovered. What to look for in a non-custodial wallet Bron’s report ranks its twelve criteria by points. Each works as a question to put to a wallet provider: Security (15 points): Does every transaction need a second authorization, and can funds be recovered if the vendor shuts down? Multi-user control (10): Are there separate roles, such as an approver and a view-only user? Inheritance (10): Is there a documented path for heirs that does not require handing over live credentials? Asset coverage (10): Does the wallet support the largest blockchains by market capitalization? Fiat rails (10): Can large amounts move in and out through bank transfers? Cross-chain swaps (10): Can funds move between chains inside the wallet? Trading (10): Are perpetual futures or tokenized assets available in the app? Fraud protection (5): Are there address allowlists, spending limits, delays and transaction simulation? AML screening (5): Are incoming funds checked for sanctions and illicit-funds risk? Staking and earn (5): Can assets earn yield without leaving self-custody? Support (5): Is human support available, with a published response time? Discretion (5): Can accounts be hidden, and can balances be made confidential on-chain? Gaps the report flags None of the ten wallets scored on AML screening of incoming funds, a criterion worth 5 points. Bron says no wallet in the group documents such screening. It adds that its own feature is coming but was not live as of October 2026. Bron also lists its own deductions. It lost four points on trading , because it offers tokenized US stocks and exchange traded funds ( ETFs ) but no perpetual futures. It lost two on fiat for having no card. Ledger, MetaMask, Phantom and Trust Wallet each scored 9 of 10 on trading. title: AI reputation management after a hack: why engines skip your incident report
body: AI engines quote the page that holds the claim they are writing, and after a hack, that is rarely your own post-mortem. Ledger published its response to the CryptoBilis implant attack on 15 October. By the next morning, ChatGPT was quoting it, while Google still did not show it. That morning, we asked four AI engines 10 questions about the incident, and Ledger's post appeared as a source in 5 of the 40 answers. The other 35 did not cite it. An engine treats your incident report as one source among many and cites it only when it holds the exact claim the answer needs. AI reputation management after a hack starts with writing those claims into the page. A hack ends in a week. AI keeps telling the story for months. This column is part of Crisis Memory, ICODA's November series on what ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini say about crypto brands after a crisis, with insights from Vlad Pivnev, Anastasia Marmuzevich, Anastasia Shalepina and Artyom Abbasov. Did AI quote Ledger's post-mortem? Only partly: ChatGPT cited the 15 October post in 4 of its 10 answers, Perplexity in 1 of 10, and Claude and Gemini never did. Dot chart: Ledger's 15 October post-mortem was cited in 4 of 10 ChatGPT answers, 1 of 10 Perplexity answers, and 0 of 10 Claude and Gemini answers. ChatGPT sent 24 of its 34 citations to Ledger's own sites, including the 2020 breach notice and the 2023 Connect Kit report. Claude sent 1 of its 52 there and built its answers from BleepingComputer, Help Net Security, The Hacker News and Bitquery. Perplexity cited 232 sources across its 10 answers, and Ledger's post appeared in one of them. Gemini skipped web search in 6 of its 10 answers, and none of those answers mentioned the incident. How do AI engines pick a source after a hack? An engine cites the page that contains the claim it is writing, so every claim your post-mortem leaves out gets sourced from someone else. Ledger's answers show that rule in three claims. Claim in the answer Source the engine used What we saw Chip, OS and servers were not compromised Ledger's response post ChatGPT: "Ledger says confirmed cases were devices redistributed through resellers in Southeast Asia, rather than a compromise of Ledger's servers, OS, or secure chip." How much was stolen Specter, Bitquery, crypto media 12 of 40 answers gave a figure, 9 named a source, none called it Ledger-confirmed. The post states no figure. When it happened The date on the page the engine cites Two ChatGPT answers date Ledger's disclosure to 15 October: "On October 15, 2026, Ledger disclosed a supply-chain attack". Ledger's first statement came on 9 October. In the second row, Claude gave Bitquery's $102.0M across 324 wallets and Specter's $86M+, then added: "Ledger itself said it has not confirmed the total number of affected users or the total value lost." In the third row, the post is dated 15 October and mentions no earlier statement, although Ledger had spoken on 9 October and confirmed the implant on 10 October. Does a Google ranking mean AI search visibility? No: on 16 October, ChatGPT quoted Ledger's post while Google did not show it, so rank and AI search visibility need separate tracking. For the query "ledger hack", an old phishing-campaigns page still held #2, and the 15 October response was missing. Engines run their own retrieval, so a page can be quoted before it ranks. Google's AI Overviews diverged by market too: after the news broke, they vanished from brand queries such as "ledger" in the US, UK, France and Germany, and stayed in Malaysia and Indonesia, where they cited crisis coverage within one to three days. "First hours, nobody recalls statement quality; they remember search results," said Anastasia Marmuzevich, Head of PR at ICODA. Old pages compete with the new one. ChatGPT cited Ledger's 2020 breach notice and 2023 incident report next to the new post. In the Crisis Memory prompts about Ledger, the 2020 leak appeared in 25 of 48 answers and the 2026 implant in 15. What should an incident page contain so AI quotes it? Write the page as a set of claims an engine can lift : dated milestones, confirmed numbers, who is affected and what users got back. Date every milestone: the first statement, the confirmation, and each update. A page that shows one date hands the engine that date. State what is confirmed and what is not, with numbers where you have them. Without them, engines fill the gap with Specter's $86M and Bitquery's $102M. Put the recovery in the same paragraph as the hack. In our Crisis Memory data, recovery came up in 33 of 34 Bitget answers that mention the hack, 30 of 38 for Bybit, and 11 of 45 for Kelp DAO. Turn the questions people ask into headings, such as "Were users compensated?" and "Is the device safe to use?", and answer each in the first sentence. Get one independent outlet to repeat your facts: 51 of Claude's 52 citations went to third-party sites. Check all four engines in the first week, because answers barely move afterwards. When we repeated the audit 24 days later, only 2 of 40 carried news from after 16 October. "Treat the incident page as an answer sheet: every question an engine might get about the hack should have a dated, quotable answer on it," Anastasia Shalepina, AI SEO Expert, ICODA. Method: API versions of ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Gemini with web search, US location, one run per prompt, 16 October 2026. title: XRP Closes Below $1 at Two-Year Low as Leverage Collapses
body: BitcoinWorld XRP Closes Below $1 at Two-Year Low as Leverage Collapses XRP posted its lowest weekly close in two years at about $0.97, according to Cryptopotato , a level the token had not touched since 2024. The print extended a correction that has erased more than 70% of XRP’s value since its peak in July 2025, and it came as the broader crypto market sold off. XRP closed at roughly $0.97, its weakest weekly finish in two years, with Binance leverage down to about 0.13 and open interest at about $325 million. The daily RSI is deeply oversold, but the $1 level now sits as resistance and a rebound is not confirmed. Key facts XRP’s lowest weekly close in two years came in at about $0.97. The token has lost more than 70% of its value since its July 2025 peak. Binance’s estimated leverage ratio for XRP fell to about 0.13, the lowest since November 2024. Futures open interest on Binance dropped to roughly $325 million from $1.5 billion earlier in the year. XRP’s daily RSI recently entered deeply oversold territory. XRP’s estimated leverage ratio on Binance has fallen to about 0.13, a level last seen in November 2024, while futures open interest on the exchange has shrunk to roughly $325 million from $1.5 billion earlier this year. That is a large retreat in speculative exposure. Fewer leveraged positions can mean fewer forced liquidations, which in turn might calm the kind of sharp volatility the market has seen during the selloff. Cryptopotato was careful on this point: the drop in leverage does not by itself signal an immediate recovery. It removes a source of instability, not the prevailing bearish mood. In past cycles that condition has sometimes preceded a short-term relief rally, but the indicator is a description of momentum, not a forecast. The bigger obstacle is price structure. title: Dow Jones: Wall Street Eyes Rebound as Morgan Stanley Targets S&P 500 at 8,700
body: Key takeaways Dow Jones suffers 849-point selloff amid market uncertainty Morgan Stanley forecasts S&P 500 recovery toward 8,700 Nvidia earnings and Fed policy shape equity sentiment The Dow Jones Industrial Average is facing another test of investor confidence after plunging nearly 850 points on November 17, even as Wall Street strategists increasingly argue that the broader stock market could recover over the coming year. The Dow finished Tuesday at 50,759.42, down 1.64%, while the S&P 500 declined 1.03% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.74%. The retreat extended a broader stock market correction driven by concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, corporate spending and interest rates. Why Is the Dow Jones Falling Despite Bullish Stock Forecasts? The Dow's recent weakness reflects growing uncertainty about corporate profitability and the outlook for monetary policy. Unlike the technology-heavy Nasdaq, the Dow tracks 30 established American companies using a price-weighted methodology. Changes in individual share prices, rather than market capitalization alone, determine each company's influence on the index. That distinction helps explain why the Dow can decline even when technology stocks recover, a divergence explored in the relationship between Nasdaq and Dow performance . Higher borrowing costs remain another obstacle. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5.1% on Wednesday as Federal Reserve officials warned that persistent inflation might require additional tightening. According to the Federal Reserve's official calendar , minutes from the October policy meeting are scheduled for release on November 18. Investors will examine whether policymakers remain concerned about inflation and how those concerns could influence December's interest-rate decision. The latest uncertainty follows a period when the Dow rallied more than 540 points as falling oil prices provided temporary relief. Morgan Stanley Sees S&P 500 Reaching 8,700 Despite recent selling, Morgan Stanley upgraded its global equity allocation to maximum overweight, citing improving valuations and expectations for stronger corporate earnings. The bank established an end-2027 S&P 500 target of 8,700, compared with Tuesday's close of 7,340.53. Reaching that level would represent approximately 18.5% upside from the latest closing value. The forecast is based partly on expectations that corporate earnings will continue growing, supported by wider adoption of artificial intelligence and more stable financial conditions. Goldman Sachs has also projected an S&P 500 level of 8,700, although its outlook anticipates slower earnings growth in 2027. The bullish forecasts contrast with the recent Nvidia-led technology selloff , which raised questions about whether AI-related spending can sustain current valuations. Nevertheless, the outlook concerns the S&P 500 rather than the Dow itself. A broad equity recovery would not necessarily produce identical gains across the two indexes. Can Nvidia Earnings Help Wall Street Recover? Nvidia's latest financial results provide an immediate source of optimism. The chipmaker reported a record $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and projected approximately $130 billion in fourth-quarter sales. Its strong earnings forecast helped lift NVDA shares in initial after-hours trading. However, Nvidia's influence is considerably greater in capitalization-weighted technology benchmarks than in the price-weighted Dow. That difference matters because a rally concentrated in AI stocks may support the Nasdaq and S&P 500 without generating equivalent gains across industrial, financial and consumer companies. Recent retail-sector earnings concerns also suggest that strong technology demand does not necessarily reflect confidence across the entire economy.

title: Decentralized Lottery Protocol CoinLotto Completes The Smart Contract Security Audit with CertiK and Launches on Mainnet
body: Decentralized lottery protocol CoinLotto has completed a smart-contract security audit with CertiK and launched on mainnet. Decentralized lottery protocol CoinLotto has announced the completion of an independent smart-contract security audit by blockchain security firm CertiK. The audit evaluated CoinLotto’s smart contracts, which handle ticket sales, prize pool accumulation, winner selection, and distribution across multiple blockchain networks. By pairing CertiK’s external security evaluation with public on-chain execution and cryptographically verifiable randomness, CoinLotto aims to establish a fully transparent foundation for decentralized lotteries. Verifiable Fairness and Immutable Prize Pools Traditional online lottery systems often rely on off-chain execution or centralized servers for prize draws. In contrast, CoinLotto runs its core lottery logic directly on-chain. Ticket purchases, prize pools, draw schedules, winner selection, and payouts are all recorded publicly, ensuring that any participant can verify the protocol’s operations. To guarantee unbiased outcomes, CoinLotto integrates Chainlink VRF 2.5 to supply cryptographically verifiable randomness for every draw. Winners are drawn directly from active, purchased tickets rather than requiring players to match arbitrary number sequences. A central feature of the architecture is its immutable prize pool management: Tamper-proof escrow: all entry funds are held in immutable smart contracts that prevent organizers or protocol owners from arbitrarily withdrawing or redirecting assets. Fixed rules: each lottery's parameters are set permanently at creation. Complete winner allocations: upon draw finalization, 100% of the calculated final prize pool is allocated to winning tickets under predefined rules without manual operator intervention. Permissionless Infrastructure for Community Lotteries Beyond operating its native protocol lotteries, CoinLotto functions as a permissionless platform where projects, creators, and Web3 communities can launch custom lotteries. Organizers can configure the following parameters using CoinLotto’s underlying on-chain infrastructure: Flexible parameters: creators set the entry token, ticket price, ticket limit, draw date, and distribution model. Custom fees: organizers can retain a Creator Fee of up to 30%. Prize models: support for three distinct payout structures – tier (predefined winning positions), win rate (target percentage of winning tickets), and multiplier (target payout relative to ticket cost). Sponsorship top-ups: external wallets can deposit extra funds into active prize pools without triggering Protocol or Creator fees, allowing sponsors to boost rewards directly. Ecosystem Mechanics and Multi-Chain Support The protocol introduces three interconnected types of lotteries: Protocol lotteries: maintained directly by CoinLotto. Every ticket issued, whether winning or non-winning, earns players $CLT tokens. Super lotteries: high-tier events players can only enter using $CLT tokens. These events are funded by 10% of ticket revenue from linked protocol lotteries as well as direct top-ups. User-created lotteries: custom lotteries deployed by users utilizing their preferred tokens. CoinLotto features permanent, on-chain referral tracking. Once registered, referral relationships cannot be overwritten or changed. Referrers automatically earn 50% of Protocol Fees generated by their invites, 10 $CLT upon an invitee's first Protocol ticket purchase, and a 5% bonus on all $CLT earned by referred players. To broaden access, CoinLotto supports BNB Chain, Base, and Ethereum, allowing projects across major EVM-compatible ecosystems to leverage its infrastructure. Additionally, all claimable funds, referral commissions, and earned $CLT tokens carry no expiration dates, allowing users to claim their funds at any time directly through on-chain transactions. About CoinLotto CoinLotto is a multi-chain decentralized lottery protocol designed to bring complete transparency, verifiable randomness, and permissionless gaming infrastructure to Web3. Built on immutable smart contracts and powered by Chainlink VRF 2.5, CoinLotto enables players, creators, and communities to participate in and launch custom lotteries across BNB Chain, Base, and Ethereum. For more information, visit the official documentation at docs.coinlotto.xyz . That is why CertiK brings together formal verification, security auditing, continuous monitoring, risk intelligence, and compliance capabilities within a unified risk management framework. Our goal is not simply to identify vulnerabilities. It is to reduce risk exposure across the digital asset lifecycle, moving organizations from reactive patching toward proactive and continuous risk management.
